content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to integrate a new [article_no] module as an additional slave in a system where a [article_no] master program is running? Currently, we have a [article_no] master and slave setup, and plan to add another board with the new [article_no] module. I can configure network inputs and outputs and upload the program—the module operates, but communication fails.
It should be feasible but with certain limitations. Please upload your program files in a ZIP archive.
Thank you. The new module ([article_no]) is identified with IP ending in ...23. If I move the master program to the new module, communication stops.

This appears to be just the program for the [article_no] master. Where is the program for the [article_no]? It seems a [article_no] master cannot establish a connection to a [article_no] slave. You may need to reconfigure your system: set [article_no] as master and both [article_no] modules as slaves.
Thank you for checking. It may be simpler to update all units to [article_no] modules, since the current setup has been operating for over a decade.
If there are expansion modules for the [article_no], they must also be replaced. The [article_no] expansion modules are not compatible with [article_no] controllers.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are trying to incorporate a newer [product_name] module as a slave into an existing [product_name] master-slave setup. Attempts to add the new module led to communication issues. Advice provided states that direct master-slave connectivity between the older and newer [product_name] modules is not supported, recommending a system reconfiguration with the newer module as the master. Additionally, expansion modules for older [product_name] units are incompatible with newer ones, complicating upgrade and expansion plans.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates adding a newer [product_name] module as a simple slave to the current [product_name] master-slave configuration without significant reconfiguration or compatibility obstacles.
